rationale: The assistant asked exactly the right first question ('check if the smell resembles rotting food or burning plastic') and, once the customer described a hot-plastic electrical smell, warm plug and buzzing, correctly told her to unplug immediately and not use it again until a qualified engineer has inspected it, with no DIY on live parts. It never asked for make, model, age or serial, so it missed the chance to steer her to the Beko fridge-freezer safety notice/manufacturer line and did not mention moving food or calling the fire service if smoke or flames appear. The candidate causes offered ('failing start relay, damaged internal wiring, or a compressor issue') were framed as possibilities rather than a confident diagnosis, and no parts were recommended. Overall a safe, useful escalation, but incomplete on the recall angle.
